cells.tense: The first concrete piece has arrived, and you are holding it level while you think.
cells.act: hold someone else up with what you have
cells.ask: Someone near you is holding more than they can carry alone. Take one whole piece of it off them this week — the form filled, the call made, the box moved — and stop when it's done.
cells.core:
Something concrete is ready to start — a first version, a resource, an offer not yet spent. You can hold a thing level without squeezing it, and that has a floor under it. Where others sway, you stay. Half a year out, what you have is still with you, and the room around it hasn't fallen in.

It isn't bearing up under a burden. It's staying steady because the thing is yours to carry. Someone near you is holding more than they can carry alone — take one whole piece of it off them this week, and stop when it's done. No follow-up, no checking. The weight eases after the piece is finished, not before. What sits with you afterward is yours to keep.

cells.verb: bringing a clear shape to the first thing and holding it steady
cells.place: a load-bearing place in someone's hands

cells.tense: You are bracing for what this could become, and the bracing works harder than the holding.
cells.act: name every feeling in it on one page, none of them crossed out
cells.ask: Let every feeling this stirs land on one page — each colour of it, nothing ruled out. When the page is full, fold it and set it aside for the day.
cells.core:
What you're holding has been held so carefully it hasn't been set down. You're not moving it; you're watching it, because the version where it goes right is still being rehearsed. Each round of bracing feels like progress. Nothing is actually moving.

There's nothing wrong with the concern. But a thing kept at arm's length can't be finished, and the rehearsal has a grip on you now. Let every feeling land on one page, nothing ruled out. That's not planning. It's letting the whole of what you feel be complete, so the grip has somewhere to go. Fold the page, set it aside, and see what's actually before you.

cells.tense: A door closed behind you and your attention is still standing at it.
cells.act: lay every piece of it out where you can see all of it at once
cells.ask: Spread everything you know about the thing you keep circling across one page, nothing held back. Read it through once, then settle one small question about it.
cells.core:
Something concrete was ready to begin, and you didn't step into it. The weight lands here, and your answering is thinner than it was, so what you bear gets the tired version instead of the clear one. You're still carrying it. What's faded is the standing.

You don't need to push harder. What's low doesn't take effort — it takes seeing. Spread everything you know about the thing you keep circling across one page, nothing kept in your head. Read it through once. A clear look is what shows you a direction, and one small decision the same day. That's not a feeling to summon. It's a page, and a page is something you can do.
cells.sheetLine: You're still carrying it, but the standing has faded.

cells.tense: You have already put something in motion, and you keep calling it the situation.
cells.act: see it whole, with nothing hidden
cells.ask: The thing you carry got there by a choice. Put the name on it on one line: what it is, and what you want from it. Nothing below the line.
cells.core:
You can take what's hard and still see it clear, and you've been filing that under just being realistic. Your grip on it is real and your judgment is good, but you're folding your part into the circumstance. You kept it. Something concrete is already here because you decided to carry it.

What you want belongs to you too, with no plan attached. The thing you carry got there by a choice — put the name on it on one line: what it is, and what you want from it. Nothing below the line, no one told. The people on the other side already know who's carrying it. The name missing from it is your own, and putting it there is a line, not a project.

The sentence that serves me more than them is 'people can count on you' — I've kept it out of the core.
